Switch

Light

Follow the run Notify on failure Read the knowledge graph

Dark

Follow the run Notify on failure Read the knowledge graph

A setting that takes effect the moment it is thrown. There is no Save, no confirmation, and no third value: the control *is* the state, and the state is boolean.

Use a checkbox when the value is one entry in a set the person submits later, and a segmented control when there are three or more choices. A switch that needs an explainer sentence under it is the wrong control, or the wrong label.

Anatomy

| Part | Class | Required | |---|---|---| | Track | .ds-switch | yes — role="switch", aria-checked, and a name from aria-label or aria-labelledby | | Thumb | .ds-switch-thumb | yes — aria-hidden, purely the position indicator |

The track is 32x18 with a 12px thumb inset 2px from whichever end it rests against, so the whole control clears size.hit-target-min on its short axis once its row padding is counted.

The off-state hairline is an inset shadow rather than a border. A border would take 1px out of the box on the off state only — the thumb would then sit 1px further in when off than when on — and it would pop in and out on toggle instead of crossfading. As a shadow it is free of layout, and it composes with the focus ring rather than replacing it.

There is no label part. The name is the consumer's own text, pointed at with aria-labelledby, or an aria-label when the control is genuinely alone.

Variants

None. One size, one shape, one accent.

A small variant is a rejected idea: the control is already at the floor of what reads in a dense row. A tone variant is also rejected — the fill is the one accent, and a red or amber switch would be a state a person must act on, which belongs in a notice rather than in a setting.

States

| State | Treatment | |---|---| | Off | bg.active fill, border.default hairline, thumb in text.primary at the leading end | | On | accent.primary fill, hairline faded to transparent, thumb in text.on-accent at the trailing end | | Pressed | Thumb stretches to 15px, anchored at the end it is resting against | | Focus | focus-ring, from :focus-visible only | | Disabled | 45% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no press stretch |

The thumb's ink follows the surface under it: text.on-accent on the accent fill, text.primary on the neutral one. A statically light thumb vanishes on any theme whose accent is itself bright.

Travel runs at motion.duration.normal on the standard ease — slow enough to be read as movement rather than a jump. The fill, the hairline, and the thumb's ink all crossfade at fast, so the colour has settled by the time the thumb lands. The press stretch is one detail, not a spring: 3px, anchored, gone on release.

Usage

It commits immediately. Never pair a switch with a Save button, and never put one in a form that submits later — that is a checkbox. If the write can fail, the row owns the failure: show the error next to the control and put the switch back where it was.

Label the setting, not the state. "Notify on failure", not "Notifications are on" — the control already says which way it is thrown, and a label that restates it goes stale the moment it is toggled.

No caption under it. A switch whose meaning needs a sentence is a naming problem. Rewrite the label.

Disabled means unavailable, not forbidden. Disable only when the setting genuinely cannot apply — its dependency is missing, the workspace has no such capability. When a person merely lacks permission, say so where the row can be read rather than presenting a dead control.

One per row. Two switches on the same row are two settings sharing one label, and neither is named.

Rebuilding it in a framework: it is a <button>, never an <input type="checkbox"> with the box hidden. The checkbox carries the wrong role and the wrong keyboard contract, and its native focus outline lands on a box nobody can see. Keep the thumb a real element rather than a ::after, so the framework can key its position off the same aria-checked the accessibility tree reads.

Accessibility

  • role="switch" with aria-checked reflecting the live value. Not aria-pressed — that is a toggle button, which is a different announcement.
  • Space toggles, Enter does not. This is the ARIA switch contract, and it is the one place a switch diverges from an ordinary button: swallow Enter rather than letting it fall through to a click.
  • A name is mandatory — aria-labelledby pointing at the visible setting name where there is one, aria-label only when the control stands alone. A switch with no name announces as "switch, on" and names nothing.
  • :focus-visible, never :focus, so clicking one does not leave a ring behind on a control the pointer already answered.
  • The disabled state uses the disabled attribute, so the control leaves the tab order rather than sitting in it as an unusable stop.
  • State is never carried by the fill alone: the thumb's position says the same thing, which is what keeps the control readable when the accent and the neutral fill are close in value.
  • Every transition and the press stretch sit behind prefers-reduced-motion: reduce. Position, colour, and contrast are identical with motion off — nothing about the state is disclosed by the animation itself.
components/switch/component.css
/* Switch — extracted from the source product's Switch primitive
 * (src/renderer/src/components/ui/Switch.tsx plus the .switch-thumb rule in
 * src/renderer/src/assets/index.css). */

/* 32x18 track holding a 12px thumb at a 2px inset on both ends.
 *
 * The off-state hairline is an inset shadow, not a border: a border would eat
 * 1px of the box on the off state only, so the thumb would sit 1px further in
 * when off than when on, and the hairline would pop rather than fade on
 * toggle. As a shadow it crossfades with the fill and composes with the focus
 * ring instead of fighting it. */
.ds-switch {
  position: relative;
  display: inline-flex;
  align-items: center;
  flex-shrink: 0;
  width: 32px;
  height: 18px;
  padding: 0;
  border: none;
  border-radius: 999px;
  background: var(--sem-color-bg-active);
  box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px var(--sem-color-border-default);
  cursor: pointer;
  transition:
    background-color var(--sem-motion-duration-fast) var(--sem-motion-ease-standard),
    box-shadow var(--sem-motion-duration-fast) var(--sem-motion-ease-standard);
}

.ds-switch[aria-checked='true'] {
  background: var(--sem-color-accent-primary);
  box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px transparent;
}

.ds-switch:focus-visible {
  outline: none;
  box-shadow: var(--sem-focus-ring);
}

.ds-switch:disabled {
  cursor: not-allowed;
  opacity: 0.45;
}

/* The thumb is the one place the system animates a size. Travel reads at
 * `normal`; the ink crossfade rides `fast` with the track under it. Offsets
 * are absolute, not deltas: 2px at rest, 32 - 12 - 2 = 18px at the far end. */
.ds-switch-thumb {
  display: inline-block;
  width: 12px;
  height: 12px;
  border-radius: 999px;
  background: var(--sem-color-text-primary);
  translate: 2px 0;
  transition-property: translate, width, background-color;
  transition-duration:
    var(--sem-motion-duration-normal), var(--sem-motion-duration-normal),
    var(--sem-motion-duration-fast);
  transition-timing-function: var(--sem-motion-ease-standard);
}

/* On the accent fill the thumb takes the accent's own foreground. A static
 * light thumb disappears on any theme whose accent is itself bright. */
.ds-switch[aria-checked='true'] .ds-switch-thumb {
  background: var(--sem-color-text-on-accent);
  translate: 18px 0;
}

/* One detail, not a spring: under the press the thumb stretches 3px, anchored
 * at the end it is resting against, and settles back on release. */
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) {
  .ds-switch:active:not(:disabled) .ds-switch-thumb {
    width: 15px;
  }
  .ds-switch[aria-checked='true']:active:not(:disabled) .ds-switch-thumb {
    translate: 15px 0;
  }
}

@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .ds-switch,
  .ds-switch-thumb {
    transition: none;
  }
}

Task card

Light

Dark

Extracted from the source product's TaskCard primitive — the canonical board-card and inbox-row surface. Its family contract keeps every worklist in the product reading as one system.

Anatomy

  • The card itself is the single interactive element (a <button> or a row with one click target) on bg.surface with a border.subtle hairline and radius.control.
  • Leading: an optional 6px status dot (ds-task-card-dot). Status only — omit it when the surrounding column or text already states the status.
  • Identifier: mono, tabular numerals, font.size.meta, text.subtle.
  • Title: font.size.body at font.weight.medium, truncating to one line.
  • Trailing: display-only meta (age, count) in text.muted; never interactive.

Variants

  • Row (shown): one line, identifier and title share the baseline.
  • Card: identifier above the title, title clamps to two lines — same tokens, different stacking; rebuild per layout need.
  • Dot tones: default neutral, --good, --warn, --danger.

States

  • Hover: bg.hover only — no shadow, scale, or glow.
  • Selected (focused pane): bg.selected neutral fill, border lifts to border.default, title ink lifts to text.primary.
  • Selected (resting pane): bg.selected-resting. A board that is not the focused pane shows its selection at this tier — see patterns/selection.
  • Focus-visible: focus.ring.

Selection is neutral, never the accent, and carries no left bar. The accent is reserved for the primary action.

Usage

  • The dot is a status signal, not decoration or category color; done/healthy rows usually carry no mark at all.
  • Do not add a second interactive element inside the card; actions live in a context menu or the detail surface.
  • Keep the trailing slot to short meta (relative age, a count).

Accessibility

  • The card exposes one accessible name combining identifier and title.
  • Selection is conveyed with aria-pressed (or aria-selected in list semantics), never by the fill alone — assistive technology reads the state from the attribute, and the ink lift to text.primary carries it visually.
  • Status dots are aria-hidden when adjacent text already carries the state; otherwise give them a role="img" label.
components/task-card/component.css
/* Task card — extracted from the source product's TaskCard primitive
 * (src/renderer/src/components/ui/TaskCard.tsx), the canonical board-card /
 * inbox-row surface. Family contract: 6px status dot, mono identifier,
 * medium title, neutral two-tier selection, background-only hover.
 * Prefer components/list-row for list surfaces; this is the board card. */

.ds-task-card {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: var(--sem-space-sm);
  padding: var(--sem-space-xs) var(--sem-space-md);
  background: var(--sem-color-bg-surface);
  border: 1px solid var(--sem-color-border-subtle);
  border-radius: var(--sem-radius-control);
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-ui);
  text-align: left;
  width: 100%;
  cursor: pointer;
  transition: background-color var(--sem-motion-duration-fast) var(--sem-motion-ease-standard);
}

/* Hover is a background change only — no shadow, no scale, no glow. */
.ds-task-card:hover {
  background: var(--sem-color-bg-hover);
}

.ds-task-card:focus-visible {
  outline: none;
  box-shadow: var(--sem-focus-ring);
}

/* Selection is neutral: the accent is reserved for the primary action, so a
 * chosen card never outranks the one thing worth clicking. Two tiers, so a
 * multi-pane surface shows exactly one focused selection. */
.ds-task-card--selected {
  background: var(--sem-color-bg-selected);
  border-color: var(--sem-color-border-default);
}

.ds-task-card--resting {
  background: var(--sem-color-bg-selected-resting);
}

/* 6px status dot. Status only — never decoration or category coding. */
.ds-task-card-dot {
  flex: none;
  width: var(--sem-space-xs);
  height: var(--sem-space-xs);
  border-radius: 999px;
  background: var(--sem-color-status-neutral);
}

.ds-task-card-dot--good {
  background: var(--sem-color-status-good);
}

.ds-task-card-dot--warn {
  background: var(--sem-color-status-warn);
}

.ds-task-card-dot--danger {
  background: var(--sem-color-status-danger);
}

.ds-task-card-id {
  flex: none;
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-mono);
  font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-meta);
  color: var(--sem-color-text-subtle);
}

.ds-task-card-title {
  min-width: 0;
  flex: 1;
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-body);
  font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-medium);
  color: var(--sem-color-text-default);
  white-space: nowrap;
  overflow: hidden;
  text-overflow: ellipsis;
}

.ds-task-card--selected .ds-task-card-title {
  color: var(--sem-color-text-primary);
}

/* Display-only trailing slot (never interactive — the card is the target). */
.ds-task-card-trailing {
  flex: none;
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-meta);
  color: var(--sem-color-text-muted);
}

@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .ds-task-card {
    transition: none;
  }
}

Tooltip

Tooltip surfaces in this document: 1 Triggers: — Last shown: —

Light — hover a row and it waits; Tab into the list and it shows at once. Escape or scroll dismisses.

production-reality-gate Refuses sample data, stubbed transports, and disconnected UI state as completion evidence.

Dark — the same triggers, the same one surface. It mirrors the mode of the container it is describing.

The description for a value the surface itself cannot show: a title truncated to one line, an icon-only control's name, a path abbreviated to its tail. It elaborates what is already on screen, and never becomes the only route to a value: the detail pane, a menu, or the control's own accessible name still carries it.

One surface per document, repositioned per trigger. A list of 200 rows mounts one tooltip, not 200.

Use a popover instead when the content is interactive, a menu when it is a list of actions, and the detail pane when the value is long enough to read rather than glance at. Never a native title attribute on a control: it is unstyleable, slow, invisible to touch, and inconsistent between browsers.

Anatomy

| Part | Class | Required | |---|---|---| | Trigger | — | the consumer's own element, carrying aria-describedby only while the surface is shown | | Surface | .ds-tooltip | yes — role="tooltip", a stable id, hidden at rest | | Title | .ds-tooltip-title | no — the identifier the description elaborates |

The surface lives at the end of <body>, not beside its trigger, so it escapes every scroll container and stacking context on the page. Position comes from two custom properties the consumer writes in viewport coordinates: --ds-tooltip-top and --ds-tooltip-left.

Content is one short description — at most a couple of lines. A tooltip that needs a heading, a list, or a link is the wrong component.

Variants

None. A tooltip has one appearance, and the only optional part is the title.

There is no arrow, no tone variant, and no size variant. An error or warning tooltip in particular is a rejected idea: a state a person must act on is never disclosed on hover.

States

| State | Treatment | |---|---| | Rest | hidden — out of view and out of the accessibility tree | | Shown from pointer | Appears after ~350 ms of hover over the trigger | | Shown from keyboard | Appears immediately on :focus-visible | | Preferred side | Inline-start of the trigger, 8px clear of it, vertically centred | | Flipped | Inline-end instead, when the preferred side has no room; then clamped inside the viewport |

The surface has no entrance animation. It is neither *alive right now* nor *just changed* — the two things motion is allowed to mean — and the pointer delay already does the pacing a fade would be reaching for.

Usage

Both paths, always. Shown on pointer-over and on :focus-visible. Hover-only fails the same progressive-disclosure clause that governs row actions. :focus-visible and not :focus: clicking a control must not draw a tooltip over the thing that was just clicked.

The delay is asymmetric on purpose. ~350 ms on pointer, so crossing a list does not fire every row in turn; none on keyboard focus, because there is no crossing to absorb.

Four ways out, all of them cheap: the pointer leaves the trigger, focus leaves it, Escape, or any scroll. Scroll dismissal is not optional — a fixed surface anchored to a row that has scrolled away is pointing at nothing. Listen for scroll in the capture phase so nested containers dismiss too.

Never interactive. pointer-events: none. Anything clickable belongs in a popover, which is a different component with a different keyboard contract.

Flip, do not shrink. Prefer the inline-start side and flip when there is no room. This is load-bearing for a right-docked pane, where the natural side is off-screen.

Restate a value only when it is actually cut off. When the tooltip's job is to repeat a title the row truncated, compare scrollWidth with clientWidth and attach only when it overflows — on text that fits it repeats what the person can already read. A tooltip that instead *adds* a description the row has no room for is a different job, and that description has to stay reachable without hovering.

Touch has no hover. Anything a tooltip explains must also be reachable without one — in the detail pane, an overflow menu, or the accessible name of the control itself.

Rebuilding it in a framework: keep the single shared surface. Mounting one per row is the defect this component exists to prevent, and it is the easy mistake to make in a component tree. When a subtree forces data-mode, mirror that mode onto the surface — it sits on the body and would otherwise be lit by the document's mode instead of the container's.

Accessibility

  • The surface carries role="tooltip" and a stable id. The trigger carries aria-describedby pointing at that id only while it is shown, so a screen reader announces the description at the moment it appears rather than on every trigger in the list.
  • aria-describedby, never aria-labelledby: a tooltip describes a control, it does not name one. An icon-only button still needs its own aria-label, and the tooltip says something that label does not — the consequence of the action, not a restatement of its name.
  • The trigger must be focusable. A tooltip on a <div> nobody can Tab to is unreachable for keyboard and screen-reader users.
  • Escape dismisses, matching the overlay rule that Escape closes the topmost surface only. The tooltip never takes focus, so nothing has to be restored.
  • The surface is never the only place a value exists. It is an elaboration of on-screen content, so a person who cannot summon it loses nothing they cannot reach another way.
  • Contrast is text.default on bg.surface-raised in both modes. Do not drop the description to text.subtle to make it feel secondary — it is already secondary by being hidden.
components/tooltip/component.css
/* Tooltip — the trigger-anchored description for a value the surface itself
 * cannot show: a title truncated to one line, an icon-only control's name, a
 * path abbreviated to its tail.
 *
 * Family contract: one surface per document, repositioned per trigger, so a
 * list of 200 rows mounts one node and not 200. The consumer's script writes
 * `--ds-tooltip-top` and `--ds-tooltip-left` (viewport coordinates) and toggles
 * `hidden`; nothing else about the surface changes between triggers.
 *
 * Never interactive. `pointer-events: none` is load-bearing, not defensive: a
 * surface that can swallow a click is a popover, and the two are different
 * components with different keyboard contracts. */

.ds-tooltip {
  position: fixed;
  top: var(--ds-tooltip-top, 0);
  left: var(--ds-tooltip-left, 0);
  z-index: var(--sem-z-popover);
  /* A measure cap, not a spacing step: past ~50 characters a tooltip is an
   * article and the value belongs in the detail pane. Declared border-box so
   * the cap is the surface, whether or not the host page ships a reset. */
  box-sizing: border-box;
  max-width: 280px;
  padding: var(--sem-space-xs) var(--sem-space-md);
  border: 1px solid var(--sem-color-border-subtle);
  border-radius: var(--sem-radius-overlay);
  background: var(--sem-color-bg-surface-raised);
  box-shadow: var(--sem-shadow-popover);
  color: var(--sem-color-text-default);
  font-family: var(--sem-font-family-ui);
  font-size: var(--sem-font-size-meta);
  line-height: var(--sem-font-line-relaxed);
  pointer-events: none;
}

/* The resting state is `hidden` — an attribute, so the surface is out of the
 * accessibility tree as well as out of view. It carries no entrance animation:
 * a tooltip is neither alive-right-now nor just-changed, and the pointer delay
 * already does the pacing a fade would be reaching for. */
.ds-tooltip[hidden] {
  display: none;
}

/* The identifier the tooltip elaborates — the truncated title, restated in
 * full above the description that explains it. */
.ds-tooltip-title {
  display: block;
  color: var(--sem-color-text-primary);
  font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-medium);
}

<script>
/* Reference behaviour for the component contract in component.md. Rebuild it
   idiomatically in your framework — what must survive the rewrite is the one
   shared surface, the two show paths with their different delays, the four
   dismissals, and aria-describedby living only while the surface is shown. */

const POINTER_DELAY_MS = 350
const VIEWPORT_GAP_PX = 8

/* One surface, authored in the markup so it is visible with scripts off, then
   lifted to the body so it escapes every scroll container and stacking
   context on the page. Moved, never cloned. */
const tip = document.getElementById('ds-tooltip-demo')
tip.classList.remove('demo-parked')
tip.hidden = true
document.body.appendChild(tip)
document.querySelector('.demo-specimen').remove()

const surfacesOut = document.getElementById('demo-surfaces')
const triggersOut = document.getElementById('demo-triggers')
const lastOut = document.getElementById('demo-last')

let timer = null
/* The trigger the delay is counting down for. Without it, crossing from a
   button onto its own glyph re-fires pointerover, restarts the timer, and a
   pointer that keeps moving inside one trigger never reaches 350 ms. */
let pending = null
let owner = null

function esc(text) {
  return text.replace(/[&<>]/g, (char) => ({ '&': '&amp;', '<': '&lt;', '>': '&gt;' })[char])
}

/* Preferred side first — inline-start, so a right-docked pane's tooltip lands
   over the page and not off it. Flip only when that side has no room, then
   clamp vertically so a trigger near an edge cannot push the surface out. */
function place(trigger) {
  const anchor = trigger.getBoundingClientRect()
  const surface = tip.getBoundingClientRect()
  let left = anchor.left - surface.width - VIEWPORT_GAP_PX
  if (left < VIEWPORT_GAP_PX) {
    left = Math.min(anchor.right + VIEWPORT_GAP_PX, window.innerWidth - surface.width - VIEWPORT_GAP_PX)
  }
  const centred = anchor.top + anchor.height / 2 - surface.height / 2
  const top = Math.max(
    VIEWPORT_GAP_PX,
    Math.min(centred, window.innerHeight - surface.height - VIEWPORT_GAP_PX),
  )
  tip.style.setProperty('--ds-tooltip-left', Math.round(left) + 'px')
  tip.style.setProperty('--ds-tooltip-top', Math.round(top) + 'px')
}

function show(trigger, source) {
  const title = trigger.dataset.tipTitle
  tip.innerHTML =
    (title ? '<span class="ds-tooltip-title">' + esc(title) + '</span>' : '') + esc(trigger.dataset.tip)
  /* The surface sits on the body, outside the container it describes. Mirror
     that container's forced mode so it is not lit by the page's mode instead. */
  const scope = trigger.closest('[data-mode]')
  if (scope) tip.setAttribute('data-mode', scope.dataset.mode)
  else tip.removeAttribute('data-mode')
  tip.hidden = false
  place(trigger)
  trigger.setAttribute('aria-describedby', tip.id)
  pending = null
  owner = trigger
  lastOut.textContent = source
}

function hide() {
  window.clearTimeout(timer)
  timer = null
  pending = null
  if (owner) {
    owner.removeAttribute('aria-describedby')
    owner = null
  }
  tip.hidden = true
}

document.addEventListener('pointerover', (event) => {
  const trigger = event.target.closest('[data-tip]')
  if (!trigger) {
    if (owner || timer) hide()
    return
  }
  if (trigger === owner || trigger === pending) return
  hide()
  pending = trigger
  timer = window.setTimeout(() => show(trigger, 'pointer, after ' + POINTER_DELAY_MS + ' ms'), POINTER_DELAY_MS)
})

/* Keyboard focus shows at once: the delay exists to keep a pointer crossing
   the list from firing every row, and a keyboard has no such crossing.
   :focus-visible, not :focus — clicking a control must not draw a tooltip on
   top of the thing that was just clicked. */
document.addEventListener('focusin', (event) => {
  const trigger = event.target.closest('[data-tip]')
  if (trigger && trigger.matches(':focus-visible')) show(trigger, 'keyboard, immediately')
  else hide()
})

document.addEventListener('focusout', hide)
document.addEventListener('pointerdown', hide)
document.addEventListener('keydown', (event) => {
  if (event.key === 'Escape') hide()
})
/* Capture, so a scroll inside any nested container dismisses too — otherwise
   the surface stays put while the row it describes slides away. */
window.addEventListener('scroll', hide, true)
window.addEventListener('resize', hide)

surfacesOut.textContent = String(document.querySelectorAll('.ds-tooltip').length)
triggersOut.textContent = String(document.querySelectorAll('[data-tip]').length)
</script>
</body>
</html>

Patterns

Context rail

Context rail

Drilling into a surface replaces the rail. It never mounts a second column of navigation beside the first. One rail, in one column, at one width — and Back pinned at its bottom to restore what it replaced.

The rule: one rail, ever

The failure this prevents

DO NOT

Model pickers

Content starts three columns in. Each one is a list of things to choose, so nothing says which choice the screen is actually about.

Three navigation columns before the first word of content. A surface that seems to need two levels of rail folds the outer level into a group of the one rail, as above — never into a column of its own.

Anatomy

  • Brand row. Fixed above the rail. Outside the swap.
  • Create + narrow. The surface's New … row and its search/filter lead the rail and stay pinned while the list scrolls — the same anatomy on every surface, so there is one place to look.
  • Groups. One list, or several under quiet headings. A heading earns its place only by separating one group from another: over a lone list, or over a list whose search field already names it, it is the same word said twice.
  • Back. A rail row pinned to the bottom, below everything. It restores the rail the surface replaced, and Escape does the same. The canvas carries no back affordance — two affordances are two answers to one question.

Selection in a two-level rail

  • The rail keeps one focused selection, at bg.selected: the thing the canvas is showing.
  • A group carrying outer context — which horizon, which project, which run — rests at bg.selected-resting permanently, whether or not the rail holds focus. It answers "where am I?", and it must not compete with "what am I looking at?".
  • Mark the group, never infer it from position: which group is the outer one belongs to the surface.

Motion

  • The incoming rail slides in from its leading edge over motion.duration.normal on motion.ease.standard — opacity and one transform, nothing that reflows.
  • Replacement in the same column at the same width is precisely the change a hard cut reads as a glitch: without the slide, everything in the column changes at once with nothing to say it arrived.
  • Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce the treatment drops out entirely. A shortened slide is a stutter.

Context rail — light

The same one column, the same two tiers, from the same tokens.

<head>

<title>Context rail</title>
<link rel="stylesheet" href="../foundations/tokens.css" />
<style>
  body {
    margin: 0;
    font-family: var(--sem-font-family-ui);
    font-size: var(--sem-font-size-body);
    line-height: var(--sem-font-line-default);
  }

    padding: var(--sem-space-3xl);
    background: var(--sem-color-bg-app);

  }

    font-size: var(--sem-font-size-title);

    margin: var(--sem-space-3xl) 0 var(--sem-space-sm);
  }
  .pat-caption {
    font-size: var(--sem-font-size-meta);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-subtle);
    max-width: 62ch;
    margin: var(--sem-space-sm) 0 0;
  }
  .pat-verdict {

    border-radius: var(--sem-radius-chip);

  code {

    font-size: var(--sem-font-size-micro);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-default);

  /* ── the app frame the pattern is drawn inside ─────────────────────────── */

  .cr-frame {
    display: flex;
    min-height: 268px;
    background: var(--sem-color-bg-app);
    border: 1px solid var(--sem-color-border-subtle);
    border-radius: var(--sem-radius-shell);
    overflow: hidden;
  }
  /* The ONE navigation column. Every drilled-in surface renders its rail here,
     at this width — in the product that width is the app sidebar's own,
     user-resizable value, so there is exactly one number for it anywhere. */
  .cr-column {
    position: relative;
    width: 208px;
    flex: none;
    display: flex;
    flex-direction: column;
    overflow: hidden;
  }
  .cr-canvas {

  .cr-field {

    justify-content: space-between;
    gap: var(--sem-space-xl);
    padding: var(--sem-space-sm) 0;
    border-bottom: 1px solid var(--sem-color-border-subtle);
    max-width: 44ch;
  }
  .cr-field span:first-child {
    color: var(--sem-color-text-default);
    font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-medium);
  }

  /* Brand row: the fixed header above the rail. It does NOT participate in the
     swap — the product name is not context, it is the window. */
  .cr-brand {
    display: flex;
    align-items: center;
    gap: var(--sem-space-xs);
    padding: var(--sem-space-md) var(--sem-space-lg) var(--sem-space-sm);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-primary);
    font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-emphasis);
    letter-spacing: var(--sem-font-tracking-tight);
  }
  .cr-brand em {
    font-style: normal;
    color: var(--sem-color-accent-primary);
  }

  .cr-rail {
    display: flex;
    flex-direction: column;
    flex: 1;
    min-height: 0;
    overflow: hidden;
  }
  .cr-scroll {
    flex: 1;
    min-height: 0;
    overflow-y: auto;
    padding: var(--sem-space-xs) var(--sem-space-xs) var(--sem-space-sm);
  }
  .cr-group {
    font-size: var(--sem-font-size-micro);
    font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-emphasis);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-subtle);
    padding: var(--sem-space-sm) var(--sem-space-xs) var(--sem-space-3xs);
  }
  .cr-row {
    display: flex;
    align-items: center;
    gap: var(--sem-space-sm);
    width: 100%;
    padding: var(--sem-space-2xs) var(--sem-space-sm);
    border: 0;
    border-radius: var(--sem-radius-control);
    background: transparent;
    color: var(--sem-color-text-default);
    font: inherit;
    font-size: var(--sem-font-size-meta);
    text-align: left;
    cursor: pointer;
  }
  .cr-row:hover {
    background: var(--sem-color-bg-hover);
  }
  .cr-row:focus-visible {
    outline: none;
    box-shadow: var(--sem-focus-ring);
  }
  .cr-row-count {
    margin-left: auto;
    font-family: var(--sem-font-family-mono);
    font-size: var(--sem-font-size-micro);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-disabled);
  }
  /* The two selection tiers, straight from patterns/selection.html — a neutral
     fill, never the accent, never an edge bar. */
  .cr-row--selected {
    background: var(--sem-color-bg-selected);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-primary);
    font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-medium);
  }
  .cr-row--resting {
    background: var(--sem-color-bg-selected-resting);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-default);
  }
  /* An outer-context GROUP rests permanently: it says which container you are
     in, not what you are working on, so it never competes for the one focused
     selection — whether or not the rail holds focus. */
  .cr-group-rows--outer .cr-row--selected {
    background: var(--sem-color-bg-selected-resting);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-default);
    font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-regular);
  }
  /* Back: a rail row pinned to the column's bottom, above nothing. */
  .cr-back {
    display: flex;
    align-items: center;
    gap: var(--sem-space-sm);
    padding: var(--sem-space-sm) var(--sem-space-lg);
    border: 0;
    border-top: 1px solid var(--sem-color-border-subtle);
    background: transparent;
    color: var(--sem-color-text-muted);
    font: inherit;
    font-size: var(--sem-font-size-meta);
    text-align: left;
    cursor: pointer;
  }
  .cr-back:hover {
    background: var(--sem-color-bg-hover);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-primary);
  }
  .cr-back:focus-visible {
    outline: none;
    box-shadow: var(--sem-focus-ring);
  }
  .cr-glyph {
    width: var(--sem-icon-size-sm);
    height: var(--sem-icon-size-sm);
    flex: none;
    color: var(--sem-color-text-subtle);
  }

  /* ── the swap, driven by a checkbox so the motion is real ───────────────── */

  .cr-toggle {
    position: absolute;
    opacity: 0;
    pointer-events: none;
  }
  .cr-swap {
    display: grid;
    flex: 1;
    min-height: 0;
  }
  .cr-swap > .cr-rail {
    grid-area: 1 / 1;
  }
  .cr-toggle:not(:checked) ~ .cr-swap > .cr-rail--surface,
  .cr-toggle:checked ~ .cr-swap > .cr-rail--app {
    visibility: hidden;
  }
  .cr-toggle:not(:checked) ~ .cr-swap > .cr-rail--app,
  .cr-toggle:checked ~ .cr-swap > .cr-rail--surface {
    animation: cr-swap-in var(--sem-motion-duration-normal) var(--sem-motion-ease-standard) both;
  }
  .cr-toggle:focus-visible ~ .cr-swap .cr-swap-trigger {
    box-shadow: var(--sem-focus-ring);
  }
  @keyframes cr-swap-in {
    from {
      opacity: 0;
      transform: translateX(-10px);
    }
    to {
      opacity: 1;
      transform: none;
    }
  }
  /* The whole treatment drops out rather than shortening: a 40ms slide reads as
     a stutter, and the pattern is legible without it. */
  @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
    .cr-toggle ~ .cr-swap > .cr-rail {
      animation: none;
    }
  }

  /* ── the anti-pattern, drawn only here ─────────────────────────────────── */

  .cr-nested .cr-column {
    border-right: 1px solid var(--sem-color-border-subtle);
  }
  .cr-nested .cr-column:nth-of-type(2),
  .cr-nested .cr-column:nth-of-type(3) {
    width: 152px;
  }
  .cr-nested-tag {
    font-family: var(--sem-font-family-mono);
    font-size: var(--sem-font-size-micro);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-disabled);
    padding: var(--sem-space-sm) var(--sem-space-lg) var(--sem-space-2xs);
  }
</style>
</head>
<body>

<div class="pat-stage" data-mode="dark">
  <p class="pat-title">Context rail</p>
  <p class="pat-lede">
    Drilling into a surface <em>replaces</em> the rail. It never mounts a second
    column of navigation beside the first. One rail, in one column, at one width —
    and <code>Back</code> pinned at its bottom to restore what it replaced.
  </p>

  <p class="pat-heading">The rule: one rail, ever</p>
  <p class="pat-verdict">DO</p>
  <div class="cr-frame">
    <div class="cr-column">
      <!-- The brand row is the window, not context: it sits above the rail and
           stays put through every swap. -->
      <div class="cr-brand">sprint<em>engine</em></div>
      <input class="cr-toggle" type="checkbox" id="cr-drill" />
      <div class="cr-swap">
        <div class="cr-rail cr-rail--app">
          <div class="cr-scroll">
            <label class="cr-row cr-swap-trigger" for="cr-drill">
              <svg class="cr-glyph" viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="none" aria-hidden="true">
                <path d="M4.8 11a3.2 3.2 0 0 1 6.4 0M2 11h12M8 5.4V3.9" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round" />
              </svg>
              Horizon
            </label>
            <div class="cr-group">Projects</div>
            <div class="cr-group-rows">
              <button type="button" class="cr-row cr-row--selected" aria-current="true">multicode</button>
              <button type="button" class="cr-row">website</button>
              <button type="button" class="cr-row">relay</button>
            </div>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div class="cr-rail cr-rail--surface">
          <div class="cr-scroll">
            <!-- Outer level, folded into a GROUP of this one rail rather than
                 given a column of its own. -->
            <div class="cr-group">Horizons</div>
            <div class="cr-group-rows cr-group-rows--outer">
              <button type="button" class="cr-row cr-row--selected" aria-current="true">Q3 platform</button>
              <button type="button" class="cr-row">Mobile beta</button>
            </div>
            <div class="cr-group">Plan</div>
            <div class="cr-group-rows">
              <button type="button" class="cr-row">Type + icon ramp<span class="cr-row-count">9</span></button>
              <button type="button" class="cr-row cr-row--selected" aria-current="true">Model pickers<span class="cr-row-count">4</span></button>
              <button type="button" class="cr-row">Provider rows<span class="cr-row-count">6</span></button>
            </div>
          </div>
          <label class="cr-back" for="cr-drill">
            <svg class="cr-glyph" viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="none" aria-hidden="true">
              <path d="M13 8H3.5m0 0L7 4.5M3.5 8 7 11.5" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" />
            </svg>
            Back
          </label>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="cr-canvas">
      <h3>Model pickers</h3>
      <div class="cr-field"><span>Delivered by</span><span>sprint-1932</span></div>
      <div class="cr-field"><span>Track</span><span>Delivery</span></div>
      <div class="cr-field"><span>Depends on</span><span>Type + icon ramp</span></div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <p class="pat-caption">
    Click <strong>Horizon</strong>, then <strong>Back</strong>. The rail is
    replaced in place and slides in from its leading edge; the brand row above it
    does not move, and the canvas keeps the whole of the rest of the window.
  </p>

  <p class="pat-heading">The failure this prevents</p>
  <p class="pat-verdict">DO NOT</p>
  <div class="cr-frame cr-nested">
    <div class="cr-column">
      <div class="cr-nested-tag">app rail</div>
      <div class="cr-scroll">
        <button type="button" class="cr-row cr-row--resting" aria-current="true">multicode</button>
        <button type="button" class="cr-row">website</button>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="cr-column">
      <div class="cr-nested-tag">door rail</div>
      <div class="cr-scroll">
        <button type="button" class="cr-row cr-row--resting" aria-current="true">Q3 platform</button>
        <button type="button" class="cr-row">Mobile beta</button>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="cr-column">
      <div class="cr-nested-tag">plan column</div>
      <div class="cr-scroll">
        <button type="button" class="cr-row cr-row--selected" aria-current="true">Model pickers</button>
        <button type="button" class="cr-row">Provider rows</button>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="cr-canvas">
      <h3>Model pickers</h3>
      Content starts three columns in. Each one is a list of things to choose,
      so nothing says which choice the screen is actually about.
    </div>
  </div>
  <p class="pat-caption">
    Three navigation columns before the first word of content. A surface that
    seems to need two levels of rail folds the outer level into a group of the one
    rail, as above — never into a column of its own.
  </p>

  <p class="pat-heading">Anatomy</p>
  <ul class="pat-list">
    <li><strong>Brand row.</strong> Fixed above the rail. Outside the swap.</li>
    <li><strong>Create + narrow.</strong> The surface's <code>New …</code> row and
      its search/filter lead the rail and stay pinned while the list scrolls —
      the same anatomy on every surface, so there is one place to look.</li>
    <li><strong>Groups.</strong> One list, or several under quiet headings. A
      heading earns its place only by separating one group from another: over a
      lone list, or over a list whose search field already names it, it is the
      same word said twice.</li>
    <li><strong>Back.</strong> A rail row pinned to the bottom, below everything.
      It restores the rail the surface replaced, and <code>Escape</code> does the
      same. The canvas carries no back affordance — two affordances are two
      answers to one question.</li>
  </ul>

  <p class="pat-heading">Selection in a two-level rail</p>
  <ul class="pat-list">
    <li>The rail keeps <strong>one focused selection</strong>, at
      <code>bg.selected</code>: the thing the canvas is showing.</li>
    <li>A group carrying <strong>outer context</strong> — which horizon, which
      project, which run — rests at <code>bg.selected-resting</code>
      <em>permanently</em>, whether or not the rail holds focus. It answers
      "where am I?", and it must not compete with "what am I looking at?".</li>
    <li>Mark the group, never infer it from position: which group is the outer one
      belongs to the surface.</li>
  </ul>

  <p class="pat-heading">Motion</p>
  <ul class="pat-list">
    <li>The incoming rail slides in from its leading edge over
      <code>motion.duration.normal</code> on <code>motion.ease.standard</code> —
      opacity and one transform, nothing that reflows.</li>
    <li>Replacement in the same column at the same width is precisely the change a
      hard cut reads as a glitch: without the slide, everything in the column
      changes at once with nothing to say it arrived.</li>
    <li>Under <code>prefers-reduced-motion: reduce</code> the treatment drops out
      entirely. A shortened slide is a stutter.</li>
  </ul>
</div>

<div class="pat-stage" data-mode="light">
  <p class="pat-title">Context rail — light</p>
  <p class="pat-lede">The same one column, the same two tiers, from the same tokens.</p>
  <div class="cr-frame">
    <div class="cr-column">
      <div class="cr-brand">sprint<em>engine</em></div>
      <div class="cr-rail">
        <div class="cr-scroll">
          <div class="cr-group">Horizons</div>
          <div class="cr-group-rows cr-group-rows--outer">
            <button type="button" class="cr-row cr-row--selected" aria-current="true">Q3 platform</button>
            <button type="button" class="cr-row">Mobile beta</button>
          </div>
          <div class="cr-group">Plan</div>
          <div class="cr-group-rows">
            <button type="button" class="cr-row">Type + icon ramp<span class="cr-row-count">9</span></button>
            <button type="button" class="cr-row cr-row--selected" aria-current="true">Model pickers<span class="cr-row-count">4</span></button>
            <button type="button" class="cr-row">Provider rows<span class="cr-row-count">6</span></button>
          </div>
        </div>
        <button type="button" class="cr-back">
          <svg class="cr-glyph" viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="none" aria-hidden="true">
            <path d="M13 8H3.5m0 0L7 4.5M3.5 8 7 11.5" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" />
          </svg>
          Back
        </button>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="cr-canvas">
      <h3>Model pickers</h3>
      <div class="cr-field"><span>Delivered by</span><span>sprint-1932</span></div>
      <div class="cr-field"><span>Track</span><span>Delivery</span></div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

</body>
</html>

List surface

List surface

The anatomy every rail, column, and panel whose job is “find a thing in a list” is built from. Create, then search with one filter glyph, then one divider, then the rows. Tokens and components alone never caught the defects this pattern exists to prevent — they are all composition defects.

The anatomy

Build to this

Search sprints…
  • design-system-conformance 1 merge left
  • skills-aside 1 merge left
  • site-truth-and-impact landed Jul 29

Project, view, sort and group all live inside the glyph. It carries the accent dot because a lens is applied — collapsing the axes must never collapse the fact that one is narrowing the list. One group, so no heading over it.

Not this

All projects · 49 ⌄
Search sprints…
Recent 49
  • design-system-conformance 1 merge left
  • skills-aside 1 merge left

Three defects, all composition: a second full-width control stacked over the field it narrows; the same choice offered as a Select here and as a menu axis elsewhere; and a “Recent” heading spanning every row, which groups nothing. The divider has also drifted below the group heading, so it no longer means “the list starts here”.

Both modes

In a list-plus-detail layout the whole block above — search, glyph, and the divider under them — is constrained to the list column. Spanning the full width reads as “search this screen” while it only ever filters one column.

<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>

<style>
  body {
    margin: 0;
    font-family: var(--sem-font-family-ui);
    font-size: var(--sem-font-size-body);
    line-height: var(--sem-font-line-default);
  }
  .pat-stage {
    padding: var(--sem-space-3xl);
    background: var(--sem-color-bg-app);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-default);
  }
  .pat-title {
    font-size: var(--sem-font-size-title);
    font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-emphasis);
    letter-spacing: var(--sem-font-tracking-tight);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-primary);
    margin: 0 0 var(--sem-space-2xs);
  }
  .pat-lede {
    color: var(--sem-color-text-muted);
    max-width: 62ch;
    margin: 0 0 var(--sem-space-2xl);
  }
  .pat-heading {
    font-size: var(--sem-font-size-heading);
    font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-emphasis);
    letter-spacing: var(--sem-font-tracking-tight);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-primary);
    margin: var(--sem-space-3xl) 0 var(--sem-space-sm);
  }
  .pat-caption {
    font-size: var(--sem-font-size-meta);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-subtle);
    max-width: 62ch;
    margin: var(--sem-space-sm) 0 0;
  }
  .pat-panes {
    display: grid;
    grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(260px, 1fr));
    gap: var(--sem-space-lg);
    align-items: start;
  }

  /* ── the anatomy ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
  .rail {
    display: flex;
    flex-direction: column;
    background: var(--sem-color-bg-surface-raised);
    border: 1px solid var(--sem-color-border-subtle);
    border-radius: var(--sem-radius-overlay);
    overflow: hidden;
  }
  /* 1+2+3: create, then search with the glyph, then THE divider. */
  .rail-head {
    padding: var(--sem-space-sm);
    border-bottom: 1px solid var(--sem-color-border-subtle);
  }
  .rail-new {
    display: flex;
    align-items: center;
    gap: var(--sem-space-xs);
    width: 100%;
    height: var(--sem-size-control-sm);
    padding: 0 var(--sem-space-sm);
    margin-bottom: var(--sem-space-sm);
    border: 1px dashed var(--sem-color-border-default);
    border-radius: var(--sem-radius-control);
    background: transparent;
    color: var(--sem-color-text-muted);
    font: inherit;
    text-align: left;
    cursor: pointer;
  }
  .rail-new:hover { background: var(--sem-color-bg-hover); color: var(--sem-color-text-primary); }
  .rail-new:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: var(--sem-shadow-focus-ring); }

  .rail-find { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: var(--sem-space-2xs); }
  .rail-search {
    display: flex;
    align-items: center;
    gap: var(--sem-space-xs);
    flex: 1;
    min-width: 0;
    height: var(--sem-size-control-sm);
    padding: 0 var(--sem-space-sm);
    border: 1px solid var(--sem-color-border-default);
    border-radius: var(--sem-radius-control);
    background: var(--sem-color-bg-surface);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-subtle);
  }
  .rail-glyph {
    position: relative;
    display: inline-flex;
    align-items: center;
    justify-content: center;
    width: var(--sem-size-control-xs);
    height: var(--sem-size-control-xs);
    flex: none;
    border: 0;
    border-radius: var(--sem-radius-control);
    background: transparent;
    color: var(--sem-color-text-muted);
    cursor: pointer;
  }
  .rail-glyph:hover { background: var(--sem-color-bg-hover); color: var(--sem-color-text-primary); }
  .rail-glyph:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: var(--sem-shadow-focus-ring); }
  /* Collapsing the axes hides them; it must never hide that one is applied. */
  .rail-glyph[data-active="true"] { color: var(--sem-color-accent-primary); }
  .rail-glyph[data-active="true"]::after {
    content: "";
    position: absolute;
    top: 0;
    right: 0;
    width: 6px;
    height: 6px;
    border-radius: var(--sem-radius-pill);
    background: var(--sem-color-accent-primary);
  }

  /* 4: the rows. */
  .rail-rows { list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: var(--sem-space-2xs); }
  .rail-row {
    display: flex;
    flex-direction: column;
    gap: var(--sem-space-3xs);
    padding: var(--sem-space-xs) var(--sem-space-sm);
    border-radius: var(--sem-radius-control);
  }
  .rail-row[aria-current="true"] { background: var(--sem-color-bg-selected); }
  .rail-row-title { color: var(--sem-color-text-default); }
  .rail-row[aria-current="true"] .rail-row-title { color: var(--sem-color-text-primary); }
  .rail-row-meta { font-size: var(--sem-font-size-meta); color: var(--sem-color-text-subtle); }
  /* A heading appears only when there are two groups to tell apart. */
  .rail-group {
    padding: var(--sem-space-sm) var(--sem-space-sm) var(--sem-space-2xs);
    font-size: var(--sem-font-size-meta);
    font-weight: var(--sem-font-weight-emphasis);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-subtle);
  }

  /* the rejected shape, for contrast */
  .rail--wrong .rail-scope {
    display: flex;
    align-items: center;
    justify-content: space-between;
    width: 100%;
    height: var(--sem-size-control-sm);
    padding: 0 var(--sem-space-sm);
    margin-bottom: var(--sem-space-sm);
    border: 1px solid var(--sem-color-border-default);
    border-radius: var(--sem-radius-control);
    background: var(--sem-color-bg-surface);
    color: var(--sem-color-text-default);
  }
  .rail--wrong .rail-head { border-bottom: 0; }
  .rail--wrong .rail-rows { border-top: 1px solid var(--sem-color-border-subtle); }
  .pat-verdict {
    display: inline-flex;
    align-items: center;
    gap: var(--sem-space-2xs);
    font-size: var(--sem-font-size-meta);
    margin: 0 0 var(--sem-space-xs);
  }
  .pat-verdict[data-tone="good"] { color: var(--sem-color-status-good); }
  .pat-verdict[data-tone="bad"] { color: var(--sem-color-status-danger); }
</style>
</head>

<div class="pat-stage">
  <h1 class="pat-title">List surface</h1>
  <p class="pat-lede">
    The anatomy every rail, column, and panel whose job is “find a thing in a
    list” is built from. Create, then search with one filter glyph, then one
    divider, then the rows. Tokens and components alone never caught the defects
    this pattern exists to prevent — they are all composition defects.
  </p>

  <h2 class="pat-heading">The anatomy</h2>
  <div class="pat-panes">
    <div>
      <p class="pat-verdict" data-tone="good">Build to this</p>
      <div class="rail">
        <div class="rail-head">
          <button type="button" class="rail-new">
            <span aria-hidden="true">+</span> New sprint
          </button>
          <div class="rail-find">
            <span class="rail-search">
              <svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" width="13" height="13" fill="none" aria-hidden="true">
                <circle cx="7" cy="7" r="4.25" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.4" />
                <path d="M10.2 10.2 13.5 13.5" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round" />
              </svg>
              Search sprints…
            </span>
            <button type="button" class="rail-glyph" data-active="true" aria-label="Filter and sort — filters active">
              <svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" width="14" height="14" fill="none" aria-hidden="true">
                <path d="M2.5 4.5h11M4.5 8h7M6.5 11.5h3" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round" />
              </svg>
            </button>
          </div>
        </div>
        <ul class="rail-rows">
          <li class="rail-row" aria-current="true">
            <span class="rail-row-title">design-system-conformance</span>
            <span class="rail-row-meta">1 merge left</span>
          </li>
          <li class="rail-row">
            <span class="rail-row-title">skills-aside</span>
            <span class="rail-row-meta">1 merge left</span>
          </li>
          <li class="rail-row">
            <span class="rail-row-title">site-truth-and-impact</span>
            <span class="rail-row-meta">landed Jul 29</span>
          </li>
        </ul>
      </div>
      <p class="pat-caption">
        Project, view, sort and group all live inside the glyph. It carries the
        accent dot because a lens is applied — collapsing the axes must never
        collapse the fact that one is narrowing the list. One group, so no
        heading over it.
      </p>
    </div>

    <div>
      <p class="pat-verdict" data-tone="bad">Not this</p>
      <div class="rail rail--wrong">
        <div class="rail-head">
          <button type="button" class="rail-new">
            <span aria-hidden="true">+</span> New sprint
          </button>
          <span class="rail-scope">All projects · 49 <span aria-hidden="true">⌄</span></span>
          <div class="rail-find">
            <span class="rail-search">
              <svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" width="13" height="13" fill="none" aria-hidden="true">
                <circle cx="7" cy="7" r="4.25" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.4" />
                <path d="M10.2 10.2 13.5 13.5" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round" />
              </svg>
              Search sprints…
            </span>
            <button type="button" class="rail-glyph" aria-label="Filter and sort">
              <svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" width="14" height="14" fill="none" aria-hidden="true">
                <path d="M2.5 4.5h11M4.5 8h7M6.5 11.5h3" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round" />
              </svg>
            </button>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div class="rail-group">Recent 49</div>
        <ul class="rail-rows">
          <li class="rail-row" aria-current="true">
            <span class="rail-row-title">design-system-conformance</span>
            <span class="rail-row-meta">1 merge left</span>
          </li>
          <li class="rail-row">
            <span class="rail-row-title">skills-aside</span>
            <span class="rail-row-meta">1 merge left</span>
          </li>
        </ul>
      </div>
      <p class="pat-caption">
        Three defects, all composition: a second full-width control stacked over
        the field it narrows; the same choice offered as a Select here and as a
        menu axis elsewhere; and a “Recent” heading spanning every row, which
        groups nothing. The divider has also drifted below the group heading, so
        it no longer means “the list starts here”.
      </p>
    </div>
  </div>

  <h2 class="pat-heading">Both modes</h2>
  <div class="pat-panes">
    <div data-mode="light">
      <div class="rail">
        <div class="rail-head">
          <button type="button" class="rail-new"><span aria-hidden="true">+</span> New item</button>
          <div class="rail-find">
            <span class="rail-search">Search items…</span>
            <button type="button" class="rail-glyph" aria-label="Filter and sort">
              <svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" width="14" height="14" fill="none" aria-hidden="true">
                <path d="M2.5 4.5h11M4.5 8h7M6.5 11.5h3" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round" />
              </svg>
            </button>
          </div>
        </div>
        <ul class="rail-rows">
          <li class="rail-row" aria-current="true">
            <span class="rail-row-title">Voice dictation becomes a real module</span>
            <span class="rail-row-meta">MC-1861 · 1h ago</span>
          </li>
          <li class="rail-row">
            <span class="rail-row-title">Reviews behind one module boundary</span>
            <span class="rail-row-meta">MC-1856 · 1h ago</span>
          </li>
        </ul>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div data-mode="dark">
      <div class="rail">
        <div class="rail-head">
          <button type="button" class="rail-new"><span aria-hidden="true">+</span> New item</button>
          <div class="rail-find">
            <span class="rail-search">Search items…</span>
            <button type="button" class="rail-glyph" aria-label="Filter and sort">
              <svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" width="14" height="14" fill="none" aria-hidden="true">
                <path d="M2.5 4.5h11M4.5 8h7M6.5 11.5h3" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round" />
              </svg>
            </button>
          </div>
        </div>
        <ul class="rail-rows">
          <li class="rail-row" aria-current="true">
            <span class="rail-row-title">Voice dictation becomes a real module</span>
            <span class="rail-row-meta">MC-1861 · 1h ago</span>
          </li>
          <li class="rail-row">
            <span class="rail-row-title">Reviews behind one module boundary</span>
            <span class="rail-row-meta">MC-1856 · 1h ago</span>
          </li>
        </ul>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <p class="pat-caption">
    In a list-plus-detail layout the whole block above — search, glyph, and the
    divider under them — is constrained to the list column. Spanning the full
    width reads as “search this screen” while it only ever filters one column.
  </p>
</div>
</body>
</html>

Selection

Selection

Selection answers “what did I pick?”. Focus answers “where am I typing?”. They are different questions and never share a treatment. Selection is a neutral fill in two tiers — the accent is reserved for the primary action, so a chosen row never outranks the one thing worth clicking.

The rule: one focused selection per surface

DO

Marketplacefocus

Sources

Categories

One pane has focus and shows --selected. The other two show --resting: they remember the choice without competing, so the eye lands on the list the keyboard is driving.

The failure this prevents

DO NOT

Marketplace

Sources

Categories

Three panes shouting at once, each with an accent fill and a left bar. Nothing says which list has focus, three signals carry one state, and the accent no longer means “this is the action”. Selection never uses the accent, and never carries a left bar.

Where a left bar is still correct

Only on a collapsed icon rail, where rows are too narrow for a fill to read. Everywhere else — every content list — selection is a fill.

Selection — light

The same two tiers, from the same tokens.

Marketplacefocus

Categories
